u0: This is the normal working state: no box-fall recovery is currently owed, and the agent is free to move through the room. When not already at the exit, the objective remains to reach it while carrying the box, picking the box up first if it is not already in hand. If the box slips from the agent's hands from here, an immediate pickup on the following step becomes mandatory.
u1: The box has just fallen, so the agent owes an immediate recovery: on the very next step it must be holding the box. Being empty-handed on that next step is an irreversible failure, while picking the box up clears the obligation and returns to normal progress. Reaching the exit while already holding the box also resolves this pending recovery; reaching it empty-handed fails.
u2: The exit has been reached without the box in hand, leaving an exit-without-box condition outstanding. The agent must come to hold the box; doing so would clear the condition and restore normal progress, while remaining empty-handed leaves it unresolved. If another fall occurs while the box is not held, the situation becomes more serious.
u3: An unresolved box fall is combined with an exit-without-box condition, so the agent needs to recover the box immediately. On the very next step the box must be in hand to clear the pending issues; staying empty-handed leads to irreversible failure. If the box is held and no new fall occurs, normal progress resumes.
u4: A mandatory recovery was missed: after the box fell, the agent was not holding it on the required next step, or an unresolved fall and exit condition was left without the box in hand. This is an irreversible failure, so successful completion is no longer possible.
